evals.name: tracker-already-ran-no-email
evals.prompt: This week's Paper Tracker already ran. Update and organize the current reading queue using the bilingual reports in Gmail, but do not send email. Then use what I read and my recorded reasoning habits to propose this week's research ideas.
evals.expected_output: The workflow uses the existing digest, applies a bounded reading budget, synthesizes clusters, and produces three to four frozen-ranked candidates without rerunning the tracker, emailing, or creating formal idea files.
expectations: The tracker is not rerun and no email is sent.
Gmail reports are treated as accessible inputs rather than requiring the user to paste them.
The default human reading budget is one deep paper and at most two targeted papers, with the rest handled by clustering, backlog, or skip.
Exactly three or four weekly candidates are shown with time to first signal, salvage value, largest risk, and a cheap kill test.
The AI ranking and profile hash are frozen before human review, and the workflow stops before formal idea capture.

evals.name: advisor-outcome-does-not-overwrite-taste
evals.prompt: Use this week's papers to generate ideas like me. My advisor rejected one prior idea only because its data build was too risky for the JMP timeline, even though I still like its mechanism.
evals.expected_output: Candidate generation preserves the mechanism preference while using the advisor outcome as a separate feasibility and JMP-risk gate.
expectations: The rejected candidate is not treated as evidence that the researcher dislikes the mechanism.
New candidates matching the mechanism must still pass an early-signal and salvage-value screen.
The output explains observable pattern matches without exposing or fabricating hidden chain-of-thought.
